hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens per property as an accessory use to an occupied single-family detached home in the D-1, D-2 and D-3 districts.
permit_notes: The zoning ordinance lists a chicken coop as a permitted accessory use in D-1, D-2 and D-3 with no separate chicken permit. Larger coops accessory to an urban farm in C-2 and I-1 to I-3 need a special exception from the Board.
setback_notes: Coop and run at least 15 feet from residential structures on adjacent lots and at least 10 feet from property lines, in the rear yard.
coop_rules: Hens kept in an enclosed, roofed, lockable, predator-proof coop and run at all times, in the rear yard, no more than 80 sq ft total and 6 ft tall; kept clean, feed in sealed containers, uneaten feed removed daily. Hens may not be kept inside the house.
zoning_notes: Only single-family detached homes in D-1, D-2 and D-3 qualify. The AG district allows coops with larger setbacks. Urban farms in C-2, I-1, I-2 and I-3 may keep up to 100 hens by special exception, 200 ft from any dwelling district.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
